mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds consistently across business cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 8.0%, it signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 8.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a contraction in the housing sector amid monetary easing, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where both HOUST and FEDFUNDS decline, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply-side contraction (INDPRO < 95.0), manufacturing output declines, signaling reduced corporate production capacity and potential earnings pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising residential sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand for housing, which correlates with higher consumer spending and corporate revenue, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS rises, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the core inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5% year-over-year, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a robust labor market driving strong consumer demand, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where both PAYEMS and HOUST increase, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment recovery regime (UNRATE > 7.5% and declining), the labor market improvement signals a strengthening economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 7.5% and declining, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
